_comment: Every FFXIV mod published here, and the ones that are not published yet.
scripts/build.js turns this into public/mods/ffxiv/plugins.json, the Dalamud plugin
repository listing players add in /xlsettings. That file is only the fallback: the
Worker (src/plugins.js) serves the same URL from each repository's own release
assets so a release updates the listing without a deploy here, and falls back to the
committed file when GitHub cannot be reached.
listed=false keeps a mod off the listing but on the page: that is where a mod waits
until its repository is public. released=true says that repository has published a
release, so the fallback listing may name its download; the served listing does not
need it, because it only carries what GitHub actually answers for.

mods.name: Ghostty
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.description: Quake-style dropdown, floating windows and terminals pinned in the world, connected to shells on your own machine through ghostty-agent. /term to toggle. Works with or without Umbra; with Umbra, the Ghostty toolbar widget shows its status and a popup terminal.
mods.needs: ghostty-agent running on the machine the game runs on.

mods.name: Almanac
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Talk to a local AI model in game, with XivMcp's tools.
mods.description: Connects a model running on your own PC (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible server) to the game through XivMcp. Setup wizard with GPU-aware model recommendations, an in-game chat with threads and streaming, and a benchmark you can share with the community leaderboard. No cloud, no Python. Requires the XivMcp plugin for game tools.
mods.needs: A local model server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible API), and XivMcp for game tools.

mods.name: XivMcp
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Model Context Protocol server for FINAL FANTASY XIV.
mods.description: Exposes game state, game data and opt-in actions to MCP clients over loopback Streamable HTTP. Anything that changes your game is approved in game first. Optional Umbra toolbar widget.
mods.needs: An MCP client on the same machine (Claude Code, Codex, Almanac).
mods.pending: The repository is not public yet, so there is nothing for the installer to download. Build it yourself in the meantime.

mods.name: XivDesktop
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Launch Linux desktop apps into the game world.
mods.description: An app launcher for FINAL FANTASY XIV running under Wine on Linux. Lists the host's freedesktop applications and opens them as world panels through Ghostty's remote windows. Optional Umbra toolbar widget.
mods.needs: Ghostty and ghostty-agent, and a Linux host running the game under Wine.
mods.pending: The repository is not public yet, so there is nothing for the installer to download. Build it yourself in the meantime.

mods.name: XivArcade
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Your own classic games as game panels, with saves kept in step across your machines.
mods.description: A library for the classic games you own, for FINAL FANTASY XIV running under Wine on Linux. /arcade lists the game files in folders you choose, starts them in RetroArch on the Linux host, and shows them as world panels through Ghostty when it is installed. Every save and save state lives in one folder that Syncthing copies between your machines. It downloads no games, BIOS files or artwork.
mods.needs: A Linux host running the game under Wine, RetroArch, and your own game files. Ghostty for panels and Syncthing for save sync are optional.
mods.pending: The repository is not public yet, so there is nothing for the installer to download. Build it yourself in the meantime.

mods.name: XivWayfinder
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: A softly glowing bead and the classic pointing glove show which way to go.
mods.description: XivWayfinder points the way in FINAL FANTASY XIV: a softly pulsing bead floats a couple of yalms ahead of you in the direction to go, and the game's own white pointing glove points there too, sliding to the edge of the screen when the way is behind you. It follows, in order, a target you set with /wayfinder X Y or another plugin sets over IPC, your map flag, and your tracked quest's next step; in another zone it names the nearest aetheryte instead. With vnavmesh installed it points along the walkable path. It only points and never moves your character.
mods.needs: Nothing beyond Dalamud (API 15), on Windows or Linux under Wine. vnavmesh is optional, for walkable paths.
mods.build: tools/fetch-dalamud.sh, then tools/install-dev.sh (or dotnet build XivWayfinder.slnx -c Release)
mods.pending: The repository is not public yet, so there is nothing for the installer to download. Build it yourself in the meantime.

mods.name: XivLantern
mods.author: Johnneylee Jack Rollins
mods.punchline: Light a lantern for your friends: a friend list, 1:1 chat and channels of your own, peer to peer.
mods.description: Friends light a lantern to say they are here. Add friends with a one-time invite, see whose lantern is lit, chat 1:1 and in channels you make, and hear from the mod's author in a channel only they can post to. Peer to peer over iroh: no Lantern server, and nothing from the game is ever sent — not your character's name, world or chat; your friends see the name you type. Off until you turn it on in settings, where it says exactly who can see what (including that relays see your IP address, and how to turn them off). Blocking, rate limits and no auto-accept.
mods.needs: Nothing beyond Dalamud (API 15); the network layer ships inside the plugin as lantern.dll. Friends running XivLantern too.
mods.build: tools/build-native.sh (cargo and mingw-w64), then dotnet build src/XivLantern.Plugin/XivLantern.Plugin.csproj -c Release and tools/package.sh
mods.pending: The repository is not public yet, so there is nothing for the installer to download. Build it yourself in the meantime.
